statement: Two snowploughs start at the same moment from opposite ends of a road and clear it towards each other, each at its own steady rate. They meet after 2 hours, and by then the first plough has cleared 3/5 of the road. How long would the second plough take to clear the whole road on its own?

choices.misconception: I multiplied 2 hours by 2/5 instead of dividing by it.
I took the 2/5 that the second plough cleared as its amount per hour, so I divided 1 by 2/5.
I worked out the time for the first plough alone, 2 hours divided by 3/5.
I thought that if two ploughs meet after 2 hours, each one alone would take twice as long.

hints: What fraction of the road did the second plough clear in those 2 hours?
Together the two ploughs cleared the whole road, so the second cleared the rest. At a steady rate, its fraction of the road and its time are in proportion, so scale up to the whole road.
The second plough cleared 2/5 of the road in 2 hours, which is 1/5 of the road per hour.

solutions.reliable: When they meet, the road is fully cleared, so the second plough cleared 1 - 3/5 = 2/5 of it in 2 hours. That is 1/5 of the road per hour, so the whole road would take 5 hours. The transferable idea: in a meeting problem the shares of the work add up to one whole, and each worker's share divided by the time gives its rate.
solutions.elegant: 2/5 of the road takes 2 hours, so each fifth takes 1 hour and all five fifths take 5 hours.

whyOnTest: Rates appear as fractions of a job, and the distractors come from dividing the wrong way or answering for the wrong plough.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
